subject: Cascade switchover protocol: hosted->dedicated sizing validation & cutover windows (StratusOne)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Sullivan <tim@stratusone.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Oct 2025 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Cascade switchover protocol: hosted->dedicated sizing validation & cutover windows (StratusOne)

Tim —

Following our call last week, attaching a concise proposal for the switchover choreography we recommend for StratusOne (high level below; full runbook attached). The goal is to transfer steady-state traffic from Hosted -> Dedicated with minimal tail latency spikes and guarded capacity backstop.

Key ideas (short):
- Cascade switchover: incremental fan-in of the Dedicated fleet by shard group (5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100%) rather than single-swap.
- Traffic fingerprinting: validate request size and sequence-length distribution against the expected production sample (we'll use the CSV you provided to model queuing).
- Warm KV priming: pre-warm popular prompt prefixes into the KV cache on targeted nodes during the 25% and 60% windows.
- Throttle-backfill windows: 30-minute calibration windows between each step to observe latency and token cost.
- Fallback policy: automated region fallback to Hosted for first 15 minutes after a step if 95th percentile latency > 3× baseline.

Deliverables attached: traffic fingerprint, switchover runbook, and KV priming spreadsheet.

Proposed timing options (pick one):
1) Nightly short window (US-PST): 01:00–04:00 over two nights (low traffic)
2) Weekend long window: Saturday 02:00–10:00 (single-day, longer soak)

Please confirm preferred timing and we'll map to your procurement/ops calendar.

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: stratusone_traffic-fingerprint-20251006.csv (CSV), cascade-switchover-runbook-v1.pdf (PDF), kv-cache-priming-plan.xlsx (XLSX)

From: Tim Sullivan <tim@stratusone.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@stratusone.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Oct 2025 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cascade switchover protocol: hosted->dedicated sizing validation & cutover windows (StratusOne)

Rishi —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few quick items from our side after reviewing the fingerprint and runbook:
- We want the fan-in to stop at 60% for the first night and run a 24-hour soak before final 100% (we have persistent background jobs that spike at UTC midnight).
- Can you explicitly call out the priming window duration and the list of prefixes you intend to seed? We need to map that to our KMS authorizations.
- Procurement asks that the cutover occurs after DocuSign is complete; we expect sign-off by Friday EOD.

Tentative preferred window: Weekend long window (Saturday) if we finish sign-off. Please include a runbook step for "procurement hold" that stalls progression at each step when procurement hasn't confirmed.

—Tim
VP, Infra and AI Platform
StratusOne

Date: Tue, 07 Oct 2025 12:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cascade switchover protocol: hosted->dedicated sizing validation & cutover windows (StratusOne)

Tim — great, noted.

Answers inline: 
- Priming: plan is 45 minutes of sequential prefix seeding per shard-group at the 25% and 60% steps. We'll share the exact prefix list (top 200 prefixes) in a follow-up CSV so you can scope KMS and RBAC.
- Procurement hold: runbook includes a manual "hold" state after each calibration window — operator approval required. We'll add an automated slack pager that surfaces the hold requirement to your procurement distribution list.
- Soak: agreed on the 24-hour soak at 60% before final migration. We'll run traffic shadowing to the Dedicated nodes during soak and keep a 10% mirrored copy to Hosted for immediate fallback.

Action items (we own bolded):
- [StratusOne] Complete DocuSign signature for the Dedicated commitment (Procurement) — target: Fri EOD.
- [Redwood] Deliver prefix list for KV priming + expected CPU/GPU memory delta per shard-group — ETA: Wed 09 Oct EOD.
- [Joint] Confirm final cutover window by Thu 10 Oct.

Kimberly/Marissa/Karthik/Monica — can you confirm capacity reservations and a provisional fleet block for the weekend window if DocuSign clears? We should also plan for a spare 10% backstop in case EC2/GPU churn affects availability.

Thanks,
Rishi

Subject: Re: Cascade switchover protocol: hosted->dedicated sizing validation & cutover windows (StratusOne)

Team —

We can provision a fleet block with the following provisional sizing for StratusOne:
- Reserved nodes: 24 x A10G-equivalent (serving optimized)
- Warm pool: 3 nodes reserved for KV priming during the 25% and 60% steps
- Backstop: extra 10% (3 nodes) held in warm standby for 48 hours post-cutover

Capacity notes: replication factor and IO bandwidth are likely the gating constraints for your prefix-heavy traffic. Karthik, please validate the network egress shaping for the soak window and verify we can mirror 10% traffic without exceeding our egress budgets.

I'll lock the provisional block contingent on DocuSign — if sign-off slips beyond Friday, we should push the window to the following weekend to guarantee node availability.

-Kim
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Rishi / Team —

1) Can you confirm billing start date — do we bill on first traffic moved to Dedicated or on the first full hour after 100% completion?
2) Please include a short line in the runbook about data residency during the soak (we require logs to be retained in our VPC only).

If those are clear we will finalize quickly.

Thanks,
Sarah

Sarah / Tim —

Great — thanks for the update and for routing DocuSign. Answers: 
1) Billing: we start committed Dedicated billing at the time tokens are served from Dedicated nodes. For accounting clarity we'll record the first hour of Dedicated-serving as the billing startpoint (so if traffic advances in the 01:45–02:15 window we bill starting 01:00 for the hour containing the first Dedicated token). We'll add a short example to the billing section of the runbook.
2) Data residency: runbook v1 includes a "VPC log sink" step during soak that prevents any logs leaving your VPC. We'll append explicit log retention durations per your security team's request.

Next steps (final):
- [StratusOne] Final DocuSign signature (Procurement) — expected Fri 17:00 PST (confirmed).
- [Redwood] Deliver prefix list and CPU/GPU delta spreadsheet — sent Mon 09 Oct EOD (we hit this; file attached).
- [Redwood Ops] Lock provisional fleet block and publish the runbook with the procurement hold fragments — Kim/Monica confirm block locked.

I'll trigger the DocuSign link and mark the runbook as "ready-for-execution" once procurement confirms. See DocuSign: https://docusign.com/ENVELOPE-90123

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the Saturday window.

Rishi
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
